passages.note: Bill overview lists Mesnard as prime sponsor of SCR1040, later amended from a permanent-school-fund measure to a tipped-wage subminimum measure.

passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute if the employer can establish by the employer's records of charged tips or gratuities or by the employee’s declaration for federal insurance contributions act purposes that for each week, when adding tips or gratuities received to wages paid, the employee received not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked.
passages.note: Engrossed bill text creates a tipped-wage subminimum (up to 25% below the minimum wage, offset by tips) rather than stating any general wage-floor rule.
Senate Final Reading #2 roll call shows Mesnard voting Y as SCR1040 passed on reconsideration, 16-12-2-0-0.

rows.reasoning: Mesnard prime-sponsored and voted Yea on SCR1040 (2024), which allows employers to pay tipped workers "up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute" so long as tips bring total pay to "not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked." This is a tipped-wage subminimum carve-out, not a statement of the general wage-floor mechanism (automatic indexing, a set level adjusted by vote, a federal baseline with local choice, holding the floor, or removing it) the rungs differ on, so it establishes only a direction, not a chair.
needs_source: Mesnard's own words stating a general minimum-wage floor rule, outside the SCR1040 tipped-wage carve-out
